title: Methodus generalior numeros quosvis satis grandes perscrutandi utrum sint primi necne?

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler tests N = αa² + βb² for primality, where αβ is one of his 'numeri idonei' (convenient/idoneal numbers). Then N is prime exactly when this representation (with coprimality conditions) is the only one. A second representation N = αx² + βy² gives α(a² − x²) = β(y² − b²). Writing α = μν, y + b = μp and y − b = νq reduces this to a² − βpq = x². The free parameter s is then run through 0, ±1, ±2, …. The values S(s) = βpq form a quadratic sequence, so their first differences form an arithmetic progression. Each value is obtained by successively subtracting a difference, and one watches for a square.

This page, §45: the factors μ, ν were earlier assumed coprime, but that is to be kept only for odd factors. If α is even, both y + b and y − b must be even, so μ and ν may both be even. Example: 520 = 8·5·13 is in Euler's idoneal table, so he treats N = 40a² + 13b² in general (b odd).

§46: The basic equation is 40a² − 13(y² − b²) = 40x². Up to b → −b (which swaps the two factors), there are two cases: (μ, ν) = (10, 4) and (20, 2). This is complete: y ± b are both even and differ by 2b ≡ 2 (mod 4), so exactly one of them is 2 mod 4, and 5 must divide one of them.

§47, Case I: y + b = 10p and y − b = 4q give b = 5p − 2q. The convergent 2/1 of 5/2 gives p = 2s + b, q = 5s + 2b (check: 5p − 2q = b). The equation becomes a² − 13(2s + b)(5s + 2b) = x². Hence S(s) = 13(10s² + 9bs + 2b²) and S(0) = 26b². The first differences are 130 ± 117b, 390 ± 117b, 650 ± 117b, …, increasing by the constant 260 = 2·13·10. The subtraction starts from a² − 26b².

§48, Case II: y + b = 20p and y − b = 2q give b = 10p − q. Taking p = s, q = 10s − b, we get a² − 13s(10s − b) = x². Then S = 13s(10s ∓ b), with differences 130 ± 13b, 390 ± 13b, …, again increasing by 260.

The purpose is a finite sieve. If no square appears before the residue becomes negative, N is prime. If a square x² appears, it gives a second representation and hence a factorization.
errors: Case I difference column: the printed '130 ± 117bb', '390 ± 117bb', etc. should read 130 ± 117b, 390 ± 117b, … The difference S(s) − S(s−1) = 13(10(2s−1) + 9b) is linear in b, not quadratic. The analogous Case II column (±13b) is printed correctly.

Minor sign-convention inconsistency: §41 asks for m/n with mν − nμ = 1, but here 2/1 against 5/2 gives 2·2 − 1·5 = −1. The parametrization is also written as p = 2s + b rather than p = νs − 2nb. The concrete parametrization used is nevertheless correct (5p − 2q = b).
In Case II the ± in '13(10 ± b)' corresponds to s = ∓1. The ordering is the reverse of Case I's convention, but it is harmless because both signs are tabulated.

ideas.what: Primality test via uniqueness of representation by αa² + βb² with αβ idoneal; search for a second representation reduced to a quadratic-sequence square search
ideas.where_published: E708, E715, E719, E725 and related letters; Opera Omnia I.4; discussed by Weil, Number Theory (1984)

ideas.what: Allowing non-coprime even factors μ, ν when α is even (2-adic case split)
ideas.modern_name: 2-adic case analysis of y² − b² = αpq

ideas.what: Tabulating S by first differences in arithmetic progression (constant second difference 2βμν), subtracted successively from a² while watching for squares
ideas.modern_name: finite differences sieve for squares, akin to Fermat's difference-of-squares method

ideas.what: Worked general treatment of the idoneal number 520 via N = 40a² + 13b²
ideas.modern_name: example of idoneal number 520 in form-splitting
ideas.where_published: E719 (and 520 appears in Euler's idoneal tables, e.g. E725)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine worked instance of Euler's well-documented idoneal-number primality method. The only notable item is a printing or computational slip (117bb for 117b).
transcription_corrections: 'notetur si $a$ sit numerus par' should be 'si $\alpha$ sit numerus par' (alpha, as in α = μν = 40).
Table row s = ±2 in Case I: '13(4±b)(10±2b)' is correct; the image shows a blurred '+' for 4.
Case I difference column as printed reads 'bb' (faithful to the original), but the mathematically correct term is 117b.
